title: Redis Caching with 1-Hour TTL
summary: We use Redis as our caching layer with a default TTL of 1 hour for cached entries.

content.overview: Our team relies on Redis for application-level caching, applying a 1-hour time-to-live (TTL) policy to balance data freshness against cache hit rates.
content.details: A 1-hour TTL means cached entries are automatically evicted after 60 minutes. This duration was chosen as a middle ground — long enough to reduce origin load and latency for frequently accessed data, short enough to prevent serving excessively stale content.
content.caveats: If upstream data changes more frequently than the 1-hour TTL window, clients may receive stale data until the cache entry expires. Cache stampede risk exists when a popular key expires and multiple requests hit the origin simultaneously.
